will destroy the enemy that has killed his father, as well as himself. It is characteristic that

literary experiment and their Jacobin leanings to which Francis Jeffrey’s cool reception of

who weaves a ‘thread so fine’ to entrap Thalaba (Thalaba viii 345), and Khawla who tries
to destroy him by making a waxen image of him and burning him on a fire (see note
